texts.preamble: M/S Pawan Shree Food International Pvt ... vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 11 August, 2020 Author: Vandana Kasrekar Bench: Vandana Kasrekar 1 Mcrc-1 The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh Mcrc-17368-2020 (M/S Pawan Shree Food International Pvt Ltd Through Authorised Perso Devaliya S/O Shri Mahe Vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh) Indore, Dated : 11-08-2020
texts.facts: Heard on admission as well as I.A.No.3186/2020 which is an application for restraining the arrest of the Officers of the petitioner Company vide Crime No.398/2019 registered at Police Station Narsinghgarh, District - Rajgarh.
texts.arguments: Learned counsel for the applicant submits that in view of the provisions of sections 50 and 51 of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006, the prosecution can be launched on the direction of the Commissioner on complaint under the Food Safety and Standard Act. It is further submitted that so far as other offences under section 420 of the I.P.C. are concerned, prima facie they are not made out from the FIR. As there is no cognizable offence, hence, no FIR can be lodged and no investigation can be made. He further submits that identical issue is pending before the Principal Seat in MCRC no. 41516/2019, in which interim relief has been granted and prays for the same relief on the ground of parity. Having heard learned counsel for the applicant, without commenting anything on the merit of the case, in view of this Court, ,prima facie, the contentions advanced by learned counsel for the applicant have substance.
texts.petitioner_arguments: Learned counsel for the applicant submits that in view of the provisions of sections 50 and 51 of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006, the prosecution can be launched on the direction of the Commissioner on complaint under the Food Safety and Standard Act. It is further submitted that so far as other offences under section 420 of the I.P.C. are concerned, prima facie they are not made out from the FIR. As there is no cognizable offence, hence, no FIR can be lodged and no investigation can be made. He further submits that identical issue is pending before the Principal Seat in MCRC no. 41516/2019, in which interim relief has been granted and prays for the same relief on the ground of parity. Having heard learned counsel for the applicant, without commenting anything on the merit of the case, in view of this Court, ,prima facie, the contentions advanced by learned counsel for the applicant have substance.
